MALÉ
Settled before 1153. A trading island that kept clearing itself to make room.
137,238 people on 208 ha: 660 to the hectare.
Still rising, on land that cannot grow.
Small plots, subdivided over generations, built to seven storeys and more.
Narrow streets shared with parked vehicles, with little shade.
0.77 m² now, about 0.49 m² by 2050.
VILLIMALÉ
A village, a prison and a resort, then resettled in 1990 to relieve Malé.
6,755 people on 36 ha: 190 to the hectare.
Fell after 2014, when land for homes ran out. About 8,200 by 2050, if new social housing is built.
Compact low housing at 246 people a hectare, beside an industrial corner at 88.
Quiet and easy to walk. Inner roads are unpaved, dusty and flood.
18 m² now, about 13.5 m² by 2050.
HULHUMALÉ
Reclaimed from 1997. Its first residents arrived in 2004.
65,714 people on 497 ha: 132 to the hectare.
Planned for 100,000 in Phase 1 and 250,000 in Phase 2.
A low, open first phase beside tightly grouped towers in the second.
Streets 11 to 21 m wide. Daily needs within 400 m in Phase 1.
2.70 m² now, about 2.55 m² as it fills.
